overall: Washington DC is in the early-morning phase of a major heat event, with current temps at 75.2°F (running max 78.8°F) as of 5:45 AM ET — well below the projected afternoon peak. A Heat Advisory is in effect with heat index values forecast up to 107°F, and a slight chance of afternoon thunderstorms (20% PoP after 3 PM) introduces minor uncertainty but is unlikely to meaningfully suppress the high. Peak heating is still roughly 10+ hours away, with all models placing the TMAX near or at 16:00-17:00 ET.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in reasonable agreement with ECMWF at 99.1°F, HRRR at 100.9°F, and NBM at 97.3°F — a spread of ~3.6°F centered near 99°F, which aligns closely with the NWS official narrative of 'high near 100°F.' max_temp_prediction: Best estimate for today's TMAX is approximately 99°F, anchored by the NWP model consensus (~99.1°F mean) and NWS narrative, with HRRR suggesting a slight upside risk toward 101°F and NBM providing a downside anchor near 97°F. For the active even-bucket Kalshi market, the ensemble signal tops out at 96-97°F (32.4%), but the raw NWP and NWS data lean above that range; the 98-99°F even bucket appears underweighted relative to model guidance, and a modest probability of breaching 100°F (~11% per META model) should not be ignored. Confidence is moderate-high that the TMAX lands between 97-101°F, with 98-100°F as the most probable corridor.
